findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `safeParse` **wrapper**, but the result is written directly as `credential.key` — every Google refresh persists `{success:true,data:{…}}`, and the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse` throws. Permanent, silent credential corruption.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma` is used but never imported in the file (only occurrence of the identifier). `ReferenceError` at runtime on every Salesforce service construction — integration is dead.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Auth gate is `req.headers[…] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. With the secret unset, a header-less request yields `undefined !== undefined` → false → **authorized**. Unauthenticated writes of arbitrary OAuth credentials for any `userId`. Must fail closed when the secret is unconfigured.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — Return shape diverges by branch: sync path returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, fallback returns the provider's own shape. Google reads `res?.data` → `undefined` → `TypeError` on `.access_token`; the catch only special-cases `invalid_grant`, so refresh silently dies. Breaks precisely the configuration this PR adds.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Same divergence, cast `as HubspotToken` with no runtime check: `.expiresIn` → `undefined` → `expiryDate = NaN`, `setAccessToken(undefined)`, and the whole `Response` object persisted as `credential.key`. Nothing throws, so corruption is silent.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal `"[object Object]"` — duplicate key, last wins. The schema is really `{access_token, "[object Object]"?}`; the documented "any numeric property is the expiry" rule does not exist, and since `z.object` strips unknown keys, `.data` returns **only** `access_token` — dropping `refresh_token`, expiry, `instance_url`, `scope`. Validation goes green while the credential is gutted.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:26 — On success, mutates data to force the literal string `"refresh_token"` when none is present, and callers persist it (o365:264, salesforce:98). Next refresh sends `refresh_token=refresh_token` → `invalid_grant`, indistinguishable from a revoked grant; Google's path then marks the credential `invalid: true`. Unrecoverable without full re-OAuth.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — The `state.teamId` branch checks only *accepted membership*, then returns early. `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` at :59 is reachable only when `teamId` is falsy — always called with `null`, i.e. dead. Any rank-and-file member can install/overwrite team-wide credentials (Stripe, Salesforce, HubSpot, Teams, Webex, Tandem). Inverted placement, not omission.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — Refreshed token is persisted, then the `jsforce.Connection` is built from the **stale** `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`. The refresh is pure overhead; requests still use the expiring token.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `response.statusText !== "OK"` as the success gate. `statusText` is empty under HTTP/2 (which `login.salesforce.com` serves) and undici doesn't synthesize it → throws `HttpError(400, "")` on healthy 200s. Use `response.ok`.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Refresh + `prisma.credential.update` run unconditionally on every `getClient` — no expiry check, unlike every other integration. Token-endpoint hammering, write amplification, and concurrent instantiations race on one credential row (lost update).

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:57 — Constructor stores `this.conn` without `await`/`.catch`, while `getClient` gained four new rejection paths. Any construct-without-immediate-use is an unhandled rejection — process-level crash risk, unattributable in background jobs.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Sync fetch never checks `response.ok`. A 4xx/5xx or HTML error page is returned as if it were a token payload; combined with #6 it validates and overwrites good credentials with garbage.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — No timeout/`AbortSignal` and no retry. Node `fetch` has no default timeout, and refresh sits on the hot path of every calendar/video operation — a hung self-hoster endpoint stalls booking flows indefinitely.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Outbound POST carries no shared secret, signature, or https enforcement — only `calcomUserId` + `appSlug`. Anyone who can reach the sync endpoint can enumerate ids and harvest live access tokens.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:4` vs `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Gate mismatch: `refreshOAuthTokens` requires `userId`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` does not. For team credentials (`userId === null`) the real provider refresh runs but is then stripped by the minimum schema → team integrations silently bricked in exactly the deployments this targets.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 — Sharing mode strips `expires_in`, so `o365AuthCredentials.expires_in` keeps its old expired value and `getToken` refreshes again on the next call — unbounded refresh loop against the self-hoster's endpoint, no backoff, no signal.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 — The `console.error` logging the zod error + raw MS response was deleted, and behavior flipped from "log and continue with old credentials" to hard throw with a generic message. The residual `tokenResponse.success &&` guard is now dead code, confirming the branch wasn't replaced.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `schema.parse()` unguarded, no try/catch → `ZodError` escapes as an opaque 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with field detail. Callers can't tell "bad payload" (don't retry) from "Cal.com down" (do retry).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` unguarded on both throws, plus zero log lines in the handler. A key-rotation mismatch fails every request with an unexplained 500.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — No HTTP method gate; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the credential-write path and 500 on an undefined body instead of returning 405 + `Allow`. Sibling handlers use `defaultHandler`/`defaultResponder` for this.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Update sets only `key` and never resets `invalid: false`, and `findFirst` arbitrarily picks one row when a user has multiple credentials for the same app (common for Google/O365 multi-account). A previously-invalidated credential stays disabled forever; both cases return 200 "Credentials updated".

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — `refreshFunction: () => any` with an untyped polymorphic return is the root cause of #4/#5 — no type-level discriminator tells eight call sites which shape they got. A generic signature or normalizing both branches would have made both failures compile errors.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — Two mutually inconsistent error contracts: throws on failure *and* returns a `{success,data}` union. Call sites disagree three different ways — o365 and salesforce narrow on dead branches, Google treats the wrapper as the value (#1).
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — AES key defaults to `""` via `

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Non-constant-time `!==` on a high-value secret, and `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is used verbatim while Node lowercases incoming header names — a mixed-case config value silently yields `undefined`, feeding the fail-open path in #3.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61 — Non-atomic `findFirst` → `update`/`create` with no unique constraint or transaction. Concurrent syncs for the same `(userId, appId)` both miss and both create duplicates; downstream `findFirst` then picks non-deterministically.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:59`, `office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:60`, `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:66 — Wired to `refreshOAuthTokens` but **not** `parseRefreshTokenResponse` — still parse with provider-specific schemas. On the sync branch webex rejects, lark's `handleLarkError` throws on the missing `code` envelope, and o365video gets no `expires_in` → refresh loop. Credential sync is inoperative for these three apps.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce is the one app that got `parseRefreshTokenResponse` but bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` (direct fetch to `login.salesforce.com`) — it opts out of sync while still applying the lossy sharing-mode schema. Worst of both branches; the abstraction's coverage claim is untrue.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:5 — `JSON.parse` on an unsigned, unvalidated, attacker-controlled query param, blind-cast to `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState`, no try/catch. It carries `teamId` into credential creation with no session binding — no OAuth CSRF protection, and `teamId` may be any JSON value reaching Prisma. Now on the shared path for all 7 integrations.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:52 — Decrypted payload written to `credential.key` with no app-specific schema validation — garbage or a bare scalar surfaces much later as a parse crash deep inside CalendarService, far from the cause.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:76 — Responses are human-readable strings only — no credential id, no machine-readable created/updated discriminator, 200 for both (create should be 201), path unversioned. Callers must string-match English.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — `select: { members: { select: { userId: true } } }` is fetched and never read — only `!team` is checked. Dead select alongside a dead-parameter guard call makes the authz intent unreadable.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5` vs `decodeOAuthState.ts:5 — Byte-identical except the last line — `encodeOAuthState` parses then re-stringifies, an identity function on a string. Named as a symmetric pair, so a future "fix" to one side breaks ten `add.ts` callers.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:38 — `throw new Error(...)` instead of `HttpError`, unlike :22 in the same function — surfaces as 500 rather than 403 and dead-ends the install with no actionable message.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264`, `salesforce:92 — Dead `.success` narrowing left behind after the helper became throwing — suggests a failure path that no longer exists.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `appConfig.slug` replaced with hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"` in the OAuth `redirect_uri`, while `appConfig` stays imported and used on the lines above and below. Unrelated to the PR's intent; a slug rename now silently breaks the callback.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16 — Empty `/** */` JSDoc on the only public entry point of a self-hoster-facing webhook.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:22 — The `"calcom-webhook-secret"` default is duplicated here and in `.env.example:239` with no shared constant, while sibling flags live in `@calcom/lib/constants`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — Sync path gated on truthy `userId`, so `userId === 0` and team credentials silently bypass the sync endpoint with no signal — the "all tokens come from sync" invariant holds only for user credentials.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file) returns a raw `fetch(...)` Response object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` are truthy. But `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and provides a refresh function that returns a `HubspotToken`. Therefore subsequent code that treats it as a Hubspot token (e.g., reading `expiresIn`, `accessToken`, etc.) will see `undefined` values or misbehave. The finding’s exact downstream effects (NaN expiry, persisting Response as key) depend on code not shown in the diff, but the core defect (type/shape divergence leading to undefined token fields) is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, it performs `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` with no `AbortController`/`signal`, no timeout mechanism, and no retry/backoff. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Outbound POST carries no shared secret, signature, or https enforcement — only `calcomUserId` + `appSlug`. Anyone who can reach the sync endpoint can enumerate ids and harvest live access tokens.

The diff also shows a webhook secret mechanism for a different endpoint (`/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), but that mechanism is not used here. Additionally, the code does not validate that `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is `https://` (it will fetch whatever URL is provided). The stronger claim about “harvesting live access tokens” depends on how the external sync endpoint behaves, but the lack of any auth on this outbound token-refresh sync call is directly verifiable in the diff and is a real security weakness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `schema.parse()` unguarded, no try/catch → `ZodError` escapes as an opaque 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400 with field detail. Callers can't tell "bad payload" (don't retry) from "Cal.com down" (do retry).
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags an unguarded `schema.parse()`/`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` call that can throw a `ZodError`, resulting in a 500 response instead of a proper 400 for invalid payloads, matching the golden issue about incorrect error handling and client confusion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` unguarded on both throws, plus zero log lines in the handler. A key-rotation mismatch fails every request with an unexplained 500.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no try/catch. Both `symmetricDecrypt(...)` (e.g., wrong/rotated/empty key via `|| ""`) and `JSON.parse(...)` can throw. There is also `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` which can throw. Any of these will bubble as an unhandled exception in a Next.js API route, producing a 500 response without a controlled JSON error message; the handler itself contains no logging to help diagnose the failure. This is a concrete robustness/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — No HTTP method gate; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the credential-write path and 500 on an undefined body instead of returning 405 + `Allow`. Sibling handlers use `defaultHandler`/`defaultResponder` for this.

adjudication.rationale: The new Next.js API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` exports `handler(req,res)` but never checks `req.method`. It immediately runs auth checks and then `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. For GET/DELETE requests, `req.body` is typically `undefined` (or empty), so `zod.parse` will throw and, with no try/catch, Next.js will return a 500 instead of a proper 405 with an `Allow` header. Also, non-POST methods could reach the credential update/create logic if they include a body and pass the secret check, since there is no method gate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — Update sets only `key` and never resets `invalid: false`, and `findFirst` arbitrarily picks one row when a user has multiple credentials for the same app (common for Google/O365 multi-account). A previously-invalidated credential stays disabled forever; both cases return 200 "Credentials updated".

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the update path locates an existing credential via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })`. If the database allows multiple `credential` rows for the same `(userId, appId)` (which is plausible here since the code explicitly avoids `upsert`/`findUnique` and uses `findFirst`), then `findFirst` will pick an arbitrary matching row and may update the wrong credential. That is a verifiable correctness risk introduced by the diff. However, the claim about needing to reset `invalid: false` is not verifiable from the diff because the `Credential` model/fields (including whether an `invalid` flag exists or is used) are not shown and no code here references such a field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — `refreshFunction: () => any` with an untyped polymorphic return is the root cause of #4/#5 — no type-level discriminator tells eight call sites which shape they got. A generic signature or normalizing both branches would have made both failures compile errors.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `refreshOAuthTokens`, the return type is effectively `any` (`refreshFunction: () => any` and no explicit return type), but the implementation can return two incompatible shapes: (1) a `fetch()` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, or (2) whatever `refreshFunction()` returns otherwise. Several call sites assume a non-`Response` shape. For example, in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code does `const token = res?.data;` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. If the sync branch is taken, `res` will be a `Response` (no `.data`), causing runtime failure (and TypeScript won't flag it because of `any`). Similarly, Hubspot assigns the result to `HubspotToken`, but the sync branch returns `Response`. A typed generic/union return with discrimination or normalization would have surfaced these as compile-time errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — Two mutually inconsistent error contracts: throws on failure *and* returns a `{success,data}` union. Call sites disagree three different ways — o365 and salesforce narrow on dead branches, Google treats the wrapper as the value (#1).

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` wraps `schema.safeParse(...)` and returns the *safeParse result object* (`{ success, data, error }`), while also throwing when `success` is false. That creates an inconsistent contract: runtime guarantees it won’t return `success:false`, but the return type remains the `{success,...}` union.

This mismatch is already causing a concrete bug at a call site shown in the diff: in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` is then written to Prisma as `data: { key }`. That would store the safeParse wrapper object rather than the parsed credential payload (`.data`).

Other call sites (e.g., Office365) treat the return as a safeParse union and branch on `tokenResponse.success`, which is a dead branch after the throw. So the finding’s claim about mutually inconsistent error contracts and disagreeing call-site expectations is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — AES key defaults to `""` via `

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the decryption key is passed as `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` when calling `symmetricDecrypt(...)`. This means if the env var is unset/empty, the code will attempt to decrypt using an empty-string key rather than rejecting the request or failing fast with a clear configuration error, which is a real security/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Non-constant-time `!==` on a high-value secret, and `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is used verbatim while Node lowercases incoming header names — a mixed-case config value silently yields `undefined`, feeding the fail-open path in #3.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does compare the header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==`, but the claim that a mixed-case `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` “silently yields undefined” and “feeds a fail-open path” is not verifiable from this code. In Next/Node, `req.headers` keys are lowercased, so a mixed-case configured name would indeed likely read as `undefined`—but when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set, that results in `undefined !== <secret>` and the request is rejected (fail-closed), not accepted. Any true “fail-open” would require `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` also being unset/undefined, which the finding doesn’t establish from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61 — Non-atomic `findFirst` → `update`/`create` with no unique constraint or transaction. Concurrent syncs for the same `(userId, appId)` both miss and both create duplicates; downstream `findFirst` then picks non-deterministically.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then conditionally `update` or `create` outside any transaction. That pattern is non-atomic: two concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no row” and both execute `create`, producing duplicates unless the DB enforces a unique constraint. The code itself hints there is no suitable unique constraint by stating “Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential” (with Prisma, upsert requires a unique selector other than `id`). If duplicates exist, subsequent `findFirst` is also nondeterministic about which credential gets updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:52 — Decrypted payload written to `credential.key` with no app-specific schema validation — garbage or a bare scalar surfaces much later as a parse crash deep inside CalendarService, far from the cause.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` the request schema only validates `keys` as a string, then the handler does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and writes the resulting value directly to `prisma.credential.update/create({ data: { key: keys } })` with no app-specific shape/schema validation. adjudication_records.issue_text: .env.example:241 — Comment says the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256" but instructs `openssl rand -base64 24` — 32 *characters*, 24 bytes of entropy. Works only by accident of character-count key derivation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `.env.example` guidance for `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` stating it “must be 32 bytes for AES256”, but immediately suggests generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces 24 random bytes encoded as a ~32-character base64 string (not 32 raw bytes).
